newsitem.title: LATVIA: NARUTA IN Q1 PROFIT, SEES YR 20,000 LATS.
newsitem.headline: NARUTA IN Q1 PROFIT, SEES YR 20,000 LATS.

text.p: Naruta confectionery said on Tuesday that its first quarter profit came to 4,068 lats against losses of 9,000 lats during the first three months of 1996 and it forecast a profit of 20,000 lats in 1997.

The company's sales volume increased to 122 tonnes or 138,764 lats in the first quarter of this year against some 38 tonnes or 60,000 lats during the same period the previous year, Valdis Smeilis, the chairman of the firm's board, told Reuters.
Naruta, a secondary list stock, was also optimistic about its earnings for the year.
"What the year will be like can already be seen from the first quarter results and we plan to make 20,000 lats in after-tax profit in 1997," Smeilis added.
He also said that the company had revised its forecast for production.
"We have revised the planned volume of 600 tonnes upwards," Smeilis said.
"We will basically be producing as much as the market is ready to accept," he said.
Smeilis said that the company's 1996 losses stemmed from the Banka Baltija crash in 1995 which prevented some of its clients from paying debts of around 30,000 lats.
Naruta also lost 15,000 lats of its own money in the bank.
"The company actually worked with a profit in 1996," Smeilis said.
